content.text:
Background (from the session that started this one):
JusPrin is a desktop 3D-printing slicer, a fork of OrcaSlicer (C++/wxWidgets). Its update check (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Updates/UpdateCheck.cpp`) reads JusPrin's GitHub releases and today only shows the result in Preferences › Updates, where Download opens the GitHub release page. On 2026-11-19 Kenneth chose, for now, a card on Home that downloads the update inside the app. The person still runs the installer themselves. He also asked for this separate prototype of a full "install and restart" on Windows, to learn its real cost and risks before deciding later. Known facts: the Windows release files are an unsigned NSIS installer and a portable zip; the Mac disk image is signed and notarised; Linux is an AppImage. The repo's AGENTS.md has the build rules, including a limit on parallel build jobs on shared machines. The main checkout's working branch is `jusprin-dev`.

Task:
Prototype "install and restart" for JusPrin on Windows, on the Windows GUI test VM in GCP, and report what actually happens. This is a measurement and a throwaway prototype. Don't land it on `jusprin-dev`, open a PR or change the release workflow.

What to find out. Measure each of these on the VM; don't infer them.
1. A running JusPrin downloads the 2.0.1 Windows installer, `JusPrin_Windows_Installer_V2.0.1_x64.exe` (192 MB), from the GitHub release `jusprin/v2.0.1` of TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin, into a temp or Downloads folder, using the app's own `Slic3r::Http`. Does Windows Defender, SmartScreen or any other warning appear when the app starts that installer? The installer is unsigned. Compare with the same file downloaded through Edge and double-clicked, which carries the "downloaded from the internet" mark.
2. Does the installer accept `/S` (it is a CPack NSIS installer, built by `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/windows_package.ps1` and `packaging.cmake`)? Does it succeed when JusPrin is still running, when it has just quit, and when it is told to wait for the old process to exit? Does it ask for administrator rights (UAC), and where does it install?
3. After a silent install, can the new version be relaunched automatically (for example the installer's finish step, or a small detached step started before JusPrin quits)? Does it come up as 2.0.1 with the same projects, printers, settings and sign-in? Check `%APPDATA%` data dir and the `JusPrin2.conf` settings file.
4. The overall time from pressing the button to the new version being open, and what the person sees during it.

Start from an installed JusPrin 2.0.0 (the 2.0.0 installer from the `jusprin/v2.0.0` release). The quickest route may be a tiny standalone test program, or a debug hook in a local build, that does the download, verifies SHA-256 against the release's `SHA256SUMS.txt`, and launches the installer the way the app would (`CreateProcess`/`ShellExecute` from a process the user started). Pick whichever proves the points with the least building. Building JusPrin on the VM is slow; reuse what's there.

How to reach the VM and build there: read the memory files `windows-gui-test-vm-gcp.md` and `windows-build-on-gcp-vm.md` in `~/.claude/projects/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/memory/` first. Use the `ai-agent@tsdtechnology.iam.gserviceaccount.com` gcloud account (see `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`). Stop the VM when you're done if you started it.

Done means a short report, under 500 words, in plain sentences, with screenshots of anything Windows shows: what worked, what was blocked or warned, the exact command lines used, and what a real implementation would need, for example a Windows code-signing certificate, waiting for the old process, or UAC. Say which findings you measured and which you inferred.

Shared notes folder for this group of sessions (outside the repo; read siblings' notes there, leave hand-over notes or large findings there instead of pasting them into messages): /Users/kenneth/Library/Application Support/Claude/side-session-notes/local_967e82c4-707b-4115-b53a-ae20ea401129

Measure relaunch, data kept, timing
Write report, stop VM

---
name: windows-gui-test-vm-gcp
description: Working recipe for testing the OrcaSlicer/JusPrin GUI headlessly on a GPU-less Windows VM in GCP, and the four traps that make it fail silently.
metadata:
  type: project
---

A Windows GUI test VM for this app works in GCP with no GPU. Instance
`jusprin-win-test`, project `elegoo-backend`, zone `us-central1-a`,
n2-standard-16 (16 vCPU, 64 GB, Cascade Lake), 500 GB pd-balanced,
Windows Server 2022. Harness + full README live outside the repo
at `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/vm-harness/windows/`. Verified 2026-09-07 end to end:
launch, screenshot, scripted click, verify the UI advanced.

**Why:** four failure modes here are silent — they look like "the app has no
window" or "the app hung" rather than reporting an error, so they cost hours if
rediscovered from scratch.

**How to apply:**
- OpenGL: the app hard-requires 3.2 and Windows software rendering is 1.1. Drop
  Mesa's `opengl32.dll` + `libgallium_wgl.dll` beside the .exe. Then force
  `GALLIUM_DRIVER=llvmpipe` and `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1` — otherwise Mesa picks
  its d3d12 backend (the GCE virtual display exposes a D3D12 device) and crashes
  on the first frame.
- Never copy the whole Mesa .7z to the VM: Defender deletes it as
  Trojan:Win32/Suschil!rfn. Extract the two DLLs elsewhere, copy only those, and
  no AV exclusion is needed.
- Session isolation is the big one: display APIs, EnumWindows and
  MainWindowTitle only see the calling session's window station, so over SSH they
  report nothing and it reads as "no window exists". Run anything UI-touching as a
  scheduled task with `-LogonType Interactive`.
- Auto-logon must be re-applied on every boot; the GCE image clears the Winlogon
  values after the boot that sets them.
- Resolution needs `gcloud compute instances update --enable-display-device`
  (instance must be stopped) or you get 640x480, smaller than the app's own window.
- WebView2 runtime is absent on a clean Windows Server image; without it the app
  blocks on a modal prompt at startup. Matters especially for JusPrin's
  WebView-based UI. See [[jusprin-rebrand-seams]].

Claude Code and the Claude desktop app are both installed for `guitest`
(2026-09-08). CLI: the native Windows installer `irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1`
puts `claude.exe` in `C:\Users\guitest\.local\bin` - no Node needed, the box has
none. Desktop app: install with Anthropic's own Intune script,
`https://downloads.claude.ai/releases/enterprise/intune/Install-Claude.ps1 -Scope User`,
which resolves the official MSIX and verifies its signature and publisher identity.
MSIX deployment works on this Windows Server 2022 image. Launch the packaged app in
session 1 through explorer.exe, so it lands at normal integrity even though the
scheduled task is elevated:
`Invoke-InSession -Exe C:\Windows\explorer.exe -ArgLine "shell:AppsFolder\Claude_pzs8sxrjxfjjc!Claude"`.
Electron renders fine on this GPU-less VM with no flags.

RDP: port 3389 is open project-wide via `default-allow-rdp` (to 0.0.0.0/0 - not
narrowed yet), and RDP as `guitest` reconnects to the existing console session
rather than starting a second one. Run `./get-rdp-password.sh` in the harness to
print the current credentials; it resolves the ephemeral IP itself and verifies
the password actually authenticates before handing it to you. Do NOT use
`gcloud compute reset-windows-password` - autologon.ps1 re-syncs the account to
Winlogon\DefaultPassword at the next boot and would undo it.

autologon.ps1 used to mint a NEW random password on every boot, so any reboot
silently invalidated the RDP credentials. Fixed 2026-09-09: it now reuses the
stored DefaultPassword and only generates one when that value is absent (delete
the value and reboot to rotate deliberately). This matters because Windows
Update on this VM is set to install and restart on its own, daily at 3 AM, and
the box has also rebooted unexpectedly several times - Kernel-Power event 41,
cause not established.

Two mechanical traps: nested quoting through `winssh.sh` into `powershell -Command`
mangles almost anything non-trivial - write a .ps1, scp it, run it with `-File`.
And a PATH change made over SSH does not reach session 1's already-running Explorer;
re-set the variable from inside the session and restart Explorer, or a new terminal
there still will not find the command.

Tuned 2026-09-08, both changes measured. Windows Defender had real-time scanning
on with zero exclusions, so it scanned every object file the compiler wrote.
Excluding C:\src, C:\tools, C:\guitest plus the compiler binaries took a
small-file write benchmark from 545 to 983 files/s and reads from 979 to 2257 -
roughly 1.8x and 2.3x, for free. Re-add these if the VM is ever rebuilt.

The boot disk was grown 100 -> 500 GB. On GCE a balanced persistent disk's speed
scales with its provisioned size (140 MB/s + 0.28 per GB), so the old 100 GB disk
was capped at 168 MB/s - it was slow *because* it was small. Aggregate write went
from that 168 ceiling to a measured 262 MB/s. Resize is online: `gcloud compute
disks resize`, then `Resize-Partition` on disk 0 partition 3; C: is the last
partition so nothing blocks the extend, and no reboot is needed.

**Do not benchmark GCE persistent disk with one synchronous writer.** A single
WriteThrough stream is latency-bound and reported only 185 MB/s on the 500 GB
disk, which reads as 'the resize did nothing'. Eight concurrent writers showed the
real 262 MB/s. Use concurrent writers - that is also what a parallel build does.

RDP now prefers the H.264 codec: AVC444ModePreferred=1 (DWORD) under
HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows NT\Terminal Services, effective on the
next connection. That does not touch the real interactivity limit, which is the
~57 ms round-trip from California to us-central1; only moving the VM to a west
coast region fixes that.

The external IP is ephemeral and changes on every stop/start.

name: windows-build-on-gcp-vm
description: JusPrin builds and runs on the GCP Windows VM; the five traps that make it fail, and why the CI Windows job failing is a runner-environment problem, not a script bug.
metadata:
  type: project
---

JusPrin compiles from source on the Windows test VM and the built binary runs
with its Agent UI visible. Verified 2026-09-07 on n2-standard-16: deps 22.7 min,
slicer 23.0 min. Output is `orca-slicer.exe` (261 KB launcher) plus
`OrcaSlicer.dll` (122.7 MB). Full recipe in
`/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/vm-harness/windows/BUILDING.md`; VM setup in its README.
See [[windows-gui-test-vm-gcp]].

**Why:** four of the five failures below produce misleading errors far from
their cause, and two were self-inflicted by how the build was driven.

**How to apply:**
- Run long builds as a Windows **scheduled task** (SYSTEM / ServiceAccount), not
  over SSH — OpenSSH kills the process tree on disconnect. Never let two builds
  share a directory: that produced OpenSSL `C1033 cannot open program database`.
- Add `C:\Program Files\Git\usr\bin` to PATH so **awk** is found, or libpng
  cannot generate `pngprefix.h` (`-DPNG_PREFIX=` in deps/PNG/PNG.cmake) and you
  get a confusing `C1083` on a header that was never written.
- Set `CMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM=3.5` for CMake 4.x.
- **Do not use the CI deps artifact** — the shipped bundle predates `deps/Eigen`
  and cannot satisfy Eigen 5.0.1. Build deps from source.
- Never hard-stop the VM mid-build: doing so left 622 installed files full of
  NUL bytes and surfaced as fake syntax errors inside Boost headers.
- Qhull is deliberately excluded on MSVC (deps/CMakeLists.txt), so 24/25 is
  complete on Windows.
- To run headless, use the app's own hook rather than dropping DLLs beside the
  exe: `src/OrcaSlicer_app_msvc.cpp` loads `<exedir>\mesa\opengl32.dll` when
  system OpenGL < 2.0. Still force `GALLIUM_DRIVER=llvmpipe`.

The `Build all` Windows CI job fails at `cmake -G "Visual Studio 17 2022"` with
"could not find any instance of Visual Studio". That is a GitHub runner
environment problem, not `build_release_vs.bat` — the same script selects the
same generator on the VM and configures fine against registered Build Tools.

**MSVC rejects `this` in a nested lambda's init-capture.** Found 2026-09-07 at
commit fbe5963b: `CallAfter([self=wxWeakRef<wxWindow>(this),...])` written INSIDE
another lambda compiled on clang but failed on MSVC with 37 errors, because MSVC
bound that `this` to the enclosing closure object, so it tried to build a
`wxWeakRef<wxWindow>` from a lambda pointer
(`Tracked_class_should_inherit_from_wxTrackable`). Name the object first —
`auto* menu = this;` then capture `menu`. Watch for this pattern whenever a
deferred callback is set up from within another lambda; it is invisible on macOS.

**PowerShell splits `-m:6` (2026-10-24).** In a .ps1, `& cmake --build … -- -m:6 -v:m`
reaches MSBuild as `-m:` `6` and fails at once ("For switch syntax, type
MSBuild -help"). Quote them: `'-m:6' '-v:m'`. Also `*>>` writes UTF-16, so
Select-String on that log matches nothing; use `2>&1 | Out-File -Encoding utf8`.
A watcher built from `winssh.sh 'powershell -Command "…\"…\"…"'` silently never
matched for 3 hours — the quoting rule above applies to status checks too.
Killing "my" processes by command-line match also took out a taskhostw.exe;
kill the PIDs your own task started (and their /T trees), not a pattern.

**Shell harness on the VM (2026-11-07, app-menus).** `C:\src\JusPrin\build\tests\shell\Release\shell_integration_harness.exe` has Mesa beside it; run it from a .cmd with `GALLIUM_DRIVER=llvmpipe` and `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1` through an Interactive scheduled task as guitest; it uses its own temp data dir. Build it with `cmake --build build --config Release --target jusprin_web shell_integration_harness -- '-m:12'` (node is at `C:\Users\guitest\.local\node-v24.21.0-win-x64`). The VM has no access to unpushed commits: send them with `git bundle create f.bundle <branch> ^<vm-head>`.
- MSVC also rejects a local `constexpr` used inside a lambda that doesn't capture it (C3493; clang accepts). Make it `static constexpr`.
- On jusprin-newui b0a2fe3b08 the default suite already fails 6 checks on Windows: three failed_autosave_* checks (the harness simulates a failed save by removing write permission, and Windows ignores that on folders), earlier_model_version_available, and agent_panel_columns_tile_the_client at 1000 and 1400 DIP. Compare against that list before blaming a change.
- In PowerShell, `[IO.File]` takes relative paths from the process folder, not from Set-Location; use absolute paths. In a .cmd, `echo exit=%ERRORLEVEL%>> f` turns `0>>` into a redirect; put a space before `>>`.

# Windows GUI test VM (GCP) — working harness

Drives a wxWidgets + OpenGL desktop app on a GPU-less Windows VM in GCP,
headlessly: launch it, screenshot it, click it, verify the result.

Verified 2026-09-07 with OrcaSlicer 2.4.2 portable.

## The VM

    instance : jusprin-win-test
    project  : elegoo-backend
    zone     : us-central1-a
    machine  : n2-standard-8, Windows Server 2022, 100GB pd-balanced
    display  : virtual display device ENABLED (required, see below)
    login    : ssh as guitest with ~/.ssh/google_compute_engine

The external IP is ephemeral and CHANGES on every stop/start. Re-read it with:

    gcloud compute instances describe jusprin-win-test --zone=us-central1-a \
      --project=elegoo-backend \
      --format="value(networkInterfaces[0].accessConfigs[0].natIP)"

then update winssh.sh / winscp.sh.

## Four things that had to be solved

1. **OpenGL.** The app hard-requires OpenGL 3.2 (src/slic3r/GUI/OpenGLManager.cpp)
   and exits below it. Stock Windows software rendering reports 1.1. Fix: drop
   Mesa's `opengl32.dll` + `libgallium_wgl.dll` (from pal1000/mesa-dist-win) next
   to the .exe. Reports OpenGL 4.2 on plain CPU.

   Mesa then auto-picks its **d3d12** backend, because the GCE virtual display
   exposes "Microsoft Basic Render Driver" as a D3D12 device — and that path
   crashed on the first frame. run-app.cmd forces the CPU rasterizer with
   `GALLIUM_DRIVER=llvmpipe` and `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1`.

   Do NOT copy the whole Mesa .7z onto the VM: Windows Defender flags the archive
   as Trojan:Win32/Suschil!rfn and deletes it. Extract the two DLLs elsewhere and
   copy just those — Defender does not object to them, so no AV exclusion is
   needed. (The archive's sha256 matches GitHub's published release digest; the
   detection is a heuristic on the bundle, which also contains Vulkan layers,
   D3D12 compilers and media-foundation encoders we don't use.)

2. **A visible desktop.** A GUI app started from an SSH shell lands in a session
   with no desktop and screenshots come back black. autologon.ps1 creates a local
   admin `guitest` and sets Winlogon AutoAdminLogon so console session 1 is always
   live. Something in the GCE image clears those values after the boot that sets
   them, so startup.ps1 re-applies them on EVERY boot.

3. **Session isolation.** Display APIs, EnumWindows and Get-Process MainWindowTitle
   only see the CALLING session's window station. Run them over SSH and they
   silently report nothing — which reads as "the app has no window" when it does.
   Everything that touches the UI goes through `Invoke-InSession` in harness.ps1,
   which registers a scheduled task with `-LogonType Interactive` so it runs in
   session 1, and writes its output to a file to be read back over SSH.

4. **Resolution.** Without a GCE virtual display device the guest falls back to
   Microsoft Basic Display Adapter with no EDID = 640x480, and the app's own
   window is 760x500. Fix (requires the instance to be STOPPED):

       gcloud compute instances stop   jusprin-win-test --zone=us-central1-a --project=elegoo-backend
       gcloud compute instances update jusprin-win-test --zone=us-central1-a --project=elegoo-backend --enable-display-device
       gcloud compute instances start  jusprin-win-test --zone=us-central1-a --project=elegoo-backend

   Then 1920x1080 is available via set-res.ps1.

## Also required by this app

Microsoft Edge WebView2 runtime is NOT present on a clean Windows Server image.
Without it the app puts up a modal "WebView2 Runtime" prompt and startup blocks
forever. Installed here as 152.0.4191.66 via the Evergreen bootstrapper:

    Invoke-WebRequest "https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/p/?LinkId=2124703" -OutFile setup.exe
    .\setup.exe /silent /install

This matters more for JusPrin than for stock Orca, since JusPrin's UI is
WebView-based.

## Files

    startup.ps1      GCE windows-startup-script-ps1: OpenSSH, port 22 firewall,
                     authorized_keys, calls autologon.ps1. Runs every boot.
    autologon.ps1    Creates guitest + sets AutoAdminLogon. Idempotent.
    harness.ps1      Invoke-InSession / Take-Screenshot. Source this first.
    screenshot.ps1   Screen capture. Must run in-session.
    probe.ps1        Lists session 1's real windows to C:\guitest\windows.txt.
    focus-app.ps1    Closes leftover task consoles, maximizes the app window.
    click.ps1        Clicks the "x,y" in C:\guitest\click.txt.
    set-res.ps1      Sets 1920x1080. Must run in-session.
    install-app.ps1  Downloads the app, places the Mesa DLLs beside the .exe.
    run-app.cmd      Launches the app with llvmpipe forced, detached.
    winssh.sh        ssh wrapper. winscp.sh: scp wrapper.

## Typical cycle

    ./winscp.sh <local.ps1> guitest@<IP>:C:/guitest/
    ./winssh.sh '. C:\guitest\harness.ps1; Invoke-InSession -TaskName "X" ...'
    ./winssh.sh '. C:\guitest\harness.ps1; Take-Screenshot'
    ./winscp.sh guitest@<IP>:C:/guitest/shot.png ./shot.png

## Known gap

There is no current JusPrin Windows binary to test. The Build all workflow's
Windows job fails at `cmake -G "Visual Studio 17 2022"` with "could not find any
instance of Visual Studio"; last green Windows build was 2026-03-04 and its
artifacts have expired. Either fix that job, or install VS Build Tools on this VM
and build from the cached OrcaSlicer_dep_win64 artifact.

#!/bin/bash
ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null -o IdentitiesOnly=yes \
    -o ConnectTimeout=15 -o LogLevel=ERROR -i ~/.ssh/google_compute_engine \
    guitest@34.135.245.169 "$@"
#!/bin/bash
scp -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null -o IdentitiesOnly=yes \
    -o LogLevel=ERROR -i ~/.ssh/google_compute_engine "$@"
# Helper functions for driving a GUI app in the auto-logon console session.
# A process started from an SSH session has no desktop; a scheduled task with
# LogonType Interactive lands in guitest's live session 1 instead.

function Invoke-InSession {
    param([string]$TaskName, [string]$Exe, [string]$ArgLine = "", [string]$WorkDir = "C:\guitest")
    $a = if ($ArgLine) {
        New-ScheduledTaskAction -Execute $Exe -Argument $ArgLine -WorkingDirectory $WorkDir
    } else {
        New-ScheduledTaskAction -Execute $Exe -WorkingDirectory $WorkDir
    }
    $p = New-ScheduledTaskPrincipal -UserId "guitest" -LogonType Interactive -RunLevel Highest
    $s = New-ScheduledTaskSettingsSet -AllowStartIfOnBatteries -DontStopIfGoingOnBatteries `
             -ExecutionTimeLimit ([TimeSpan]::Zero)
    Register-ScheduledTask -TaskName $TaskName -Action $a -Principal $p -Settings $s -Force | Out-Null
    Start-ScheduledTask -TaskName $TaskName
}

function Take-Screenshot {
    Invoke-InSession -TaskName "GuiShot" `
        -Exe "C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe" `
        -ArgLine "-NoProfile -WindowStyle Hidden -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File C:\guitest\screenshot.ps1"
    Start-Sleep -Seconds 4
}

# Runs a helper .ps1 from C:\guitest inside session 1 and waits for it.
function Invoke-Helper {
    param([string]$Name, [int]$Wait = 3)
    Invoke-InSession -TaskName "Gui$Name" `
        -Exe "C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe" `
        -ArgLine "-NoProfile -WindowStyle Hidden -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File C:\guitest\$Name.ps1"
    Start-Sleep -Seconds $Wait
}
# Runs INSIDE the interactive console session (via scheduled task).
Add-Type -AssemblyName System.Windows.Forms
Add-Type -AssemblyName System.Drawing
$s = [System.Windows.Forms.SystemInformation]::VirtualScreen
$bmp = New-Object System.Drawing.Bitmap $s.Width, $s.Height
$g = [System.Drawing.Graphics]::FromImage($bmp)
$g.CopyFromScreen($s.Location, [System.Drawing.Point]::Empty, $s.Size)
$bmp.Save("C:\guitest\shot.png", [System.Drawing.Imaging.ImageFormat]::Png)
$g.Dispose(); $bmp.Dispose()

# JusPrin's package identity. The top-level CMakeLists.txt includes this file
# just before include(CPack), so each value set here replaces OrcaSlicer's.
#
# Without it the Windows installer calls itself OrcaSlicer by SoftFever,
# version 2.4.2, and uses OrcaSlicer's uninstall key. Because OrcaSlicer turns
# on CPACK_NSIS_ENABLE_UNINSTALL_BEFORE_INSTALL, that installer would first
# uninstall a real OrcaSlicer. With the key "JusPrin", the one JusPrin 1.x
# used, installing 2.x replaces 1.x instead.
#
# The macOS app and the Linux AppImage get the same identity in the release
# workflow (.github/workflows/jusprin_release.yml), which renames and edits
# them after the build.
#
# The version and publisher come from identity.cmake, which the Windows
# version resource of orca-slicer.exe reads too.

; Included near the top of the NSIS installer script CPack writes
; (packaging.cmake adds it through CPACK_NSIS_DEFINES).

; The finish page's "Run JusPrin" box. The installer runs as administrator, and
; a program it starts directly would too: Windows then blocks files dragged
; from File Explorer into it. Explorer starts JusPrin as the signed-in user.
!define MUI_FINISHPAGE_RUN_FUNCTION JusPrinRun
Function JusPrinRun
  Exec '"$WINDIR\explorer.exe" "$INSTDIR\orca-slicer.exe"'

---
name: real-app-signed-in-without-screen-control
description: "Drive the real app signed in to a local gateway through an injected page script; which conf keys, why a copied binary dies, and what still needs the screen."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: f57d8b7e-fd5a-4daf-9378-2e3d21342f7c
  modified: 2026-11-02T13:45:04.141Z
---

Builds on [[live-host-check-via-instrumented-dev-page]]; used 2026-11-02 when screen control of the app was denied.

- Signed-in conf needs all of: `jusprin_agent.{provider=jusprin, jusprin_api_key, enabled=true, cloud_consent=true, jusprin_model_formats=<JSON id→format from GET /ent/jusprin/v2/models>}`, `jusprin_server.base_url`, `jusprin_onboarding.status=completed`. Without the formats the Agent says "not set up".
- An installed printer is `"models":[{"vendor":"Custom","model":"Generic Klipper Printer","nozzle_diameter":"0.4"}]`, not `vendors`.
- Kill the app before editing the conf. Replace a scratch binary with `rm` then `cp`: `cp` over a binary that has run gets the new process killed at launch.
- `Contents/Resources` in the build is a symlink to the worktree. Replace it with a real folder of links before corrupting a resource, or the worktree gets corrupted.
- Bringing the app forward triggers an account refresh, so to race the gateway (a real 402), change the ledger and send without refocusing.
- Page text input: native value setter plus an `input` event. A modal Preferences window's page polls as `agent-preferences`.
- A test preset needs a `version` field or import rejects it.
- A compose recreate drops env set by a wrapper; check `JUSPRIN_MODEL_ALIASES` before any chat so only the fake upstream is reachable.

Still needs the screen: pointer hover, native file dialogs, Orca's wizard.

The search turned up mostly community posts, blogs, and forum threads, with few official Microsoft sources, so treat the specifics as secondhand.

**How the two mechanisms differ:** Mark of the Web is a hidden tag Windows attaches to downloaded files, and it mainly triggers SmartScreen's reputation check. One source notes that only software downloaded by web browsers or copied from network shares using Windows Explorer is likely to get a Mark-of-the-Web that results in consulting SmartScreen's reputation service. Smart App Control is a separate, stricter layer. One source says it evaluates trust/signatures of all code that is loaded by the Windows OS Loader and script engines.

**Unsigned installers:** Per one guide, SAC blocks apps and scripts that Microsoft's cloud data flags as unsafe or doesn't recognize, including unsigned installers, unknown scripts and new indie or open-source programs with no reputation. Another source adds that if reputation is unknown and the file is unsigned—or predicted malicious—the operating system blocks it outright.

**Mark of the Web specifically:** A 2022 report said Windows 11 with smart app control blocks iso and lnk files that have mark of the web just like Macros. I couldn't confirm from these results whether SAC blocks plain .exe or .msi files based on the tag alone.

**Signed installers still get blocked:** Several threads describe signed installers being blocked, including an Advanced Installer forum case and a Rhino installer report. In one Rhino case, the poster said it still blocked the installer (notwithstanding Windows File Explorer saying the signature is good!. A Microsoft Q&A answer suggests Smart App Control treats signed installers differently from loose executables.

**Recent change:** A March 2026 post reports that as of April 2026, in Windows 11 25H2, if you enable Smart App Control, the "Choose where to get apps" setting behaves as if it's set to "Anywhere". Another April 2026 post says the earlier limitation has been removed in Windows 11 version 25H2, which makes the feature easier to try out.

**Workarounds:** Sources point to a few options: remove the Mark of the Web from the file for tools you run often, check whether the file shows an Unblock option, or once Smart App Control is turned off, it may not be possible to turn it back on without resetting or reinstalling Windows. Turning SAC off is a significant security trade-off, so I'd check Microsoft's own documentation before doing it.

# Windows "install and restart" prototype: what happened on the VM

Measured 2026-11-19 on the GCP Windows test VM (jusprin-win-test, Windows Server 2022, no GPU).
It started from JusPrin 2.0.0 installed in C:\Program Files\JusPrin and the real %APPDATA%\JusPrin2 data folder,
which has 4 projects, an Anker M5 printer and an Anthropic API key. Nothing was committed or landed.
The test program is updater_proto.cpp in this folder. It compiles the app's own src/slic3r/Utils/Http.cpp
against the deps on the VM (build.cmd). The test scripts are common.ps1 and c1/c2/c3.ps1, and helper-log.txt is its log.

## Measured

- Download: `Slic3r::Http::get(<release url>)` fetched the 192 MB installer in 3.2 s. That is GCP bandwidth; a home connection will be slower.
  Checking it against SHA256SUMS.txt took 3.4 s and the sums matched.
- The downloaded file has no Zone.Identifier stream (no "downloaded from the internet" mark).
- From a normal-user process (medium integrity, started through Explorer):
  - `CreateProcessW("<installer> /S")` fails with error 740 (requires elevation). The installer's manifest says `requireAdministrator`.
  - `ShellExecuteExW(verb "open", "<installer>", "/S")` shows the UAC prompt (consent.exe). No SmartScreen step runs first.
    The prompt is on the secure desktop, so my screenshot tool could not capture it ("The handle is invalid").
- The same file with Edge's mark (ZoneId=3), opened from Explorer, shows SmartScreen's "Windows protected your PC"; "More info" shows
  "Publisher: Unknown publisher" plus "Run anyway". Downloading it in Edge first shows "isn't commonly downloaded. Make sure you trust …".
  For the double-click test I wrote Edge's mark onto a copy myself, because Edge's download panel ignored synthetic clicks.
- Defender reported no detections (Get-MpThreatDetection was empty).
- `/S` works. Fresh install: 33 s, exit 0. It installs per-machine to C:\Program Files\JusPrin, uninstall key HKLM\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\…\Uninstall\JusPrin.
  With the installer's own "Run JusPrin" step skipped in silent mode, nothing relaunches the app.
- **The app still open:** the installer exits 0 and the registry says 2.0.1, but orca-slicer.exe, OrcaSlicer.dll and ~50 other DLLs stay at 2.0.0
  while ~18,850 resource files become 2.0.1. The running app keeps going. A restart runs the mixed install. Running the installer again after quitting repairs it.
- **The app just quit:** 45 s, exit 0, every file 2.0.1.
- **Helper flow** (elevated helper waits for the app's PID, runs `installer /S`, then `explorer.exe "C:\Program Files\JusPrin\orca-slicer.exe"`):
  the app took 11 s to close, the install 136 s, the new process appeared at 152 s and the window at 190 s. The new app is not elevated (parent is Explorer).
  Same 4 projects, same printer. JusPrin2.conf is unchanged except `last_backup_path` and its checksum line. 1,841 data files before and after.
- Install time varied from 45 to 136 s for the same upgrade on this VM.
- Disk full (600 MB free, caused by another session plus my files) made `/S` exit 2 halfway. That left a half-copied folder and no uninstall entry.

## Inferred, not measured

- Windows 11 Smart App Control checks every unsigned program however it is started, mark or no mark (secondary sources only).
  Server 2022 has no Smart App Control, so this VM cannot show it.
- Http keeps the whole body in memory before on_complete; a real version should stream to a file.

content.text:
I ran the Windows "install and restart" prototype on the test VM. The full flow (wait for JusPrin to quit, install 2.0.1 silently, reopen it) took 190 s and worked, with projects, printer and settings unchanged. The biggest risk: installing while the app is still open reports success but leaves the old program files in place. Nothing was committed or landed. The report, screenshots and test program are in the shared notes folder under `win-install-restart/` (`REPORT.md`).

**How I tested.** I built a small test program that compiles the app's own `Slic3r::Http` code, downloads the 2.0.1 installer, checks its SHA-256 against `SHA256SUMS.txt`, and starts it the way the app would. The starting point was JusPrin 2.0.0 installed in `C:\Program Files\JusPrin`, using the real data folder (4 projects, an Anker M5 printer, an API key).

**Measured:**
- **Download:** 192 MB in 3.2 s on Google Cloud bandwidth (a home connection will be slower). The checksum matched.
- **No SmartScreen when the app downloads the file.** That copy has no "downloaded from the internet" mark, so no SmartScreen check ran. Defender reported nothing.
- **Warnings on the browser-downloaded copy:**
  - Edge showed "isn't commonly downloaded" when downloading it.
  - Opening it from Explorer showed "Windows protected your PC", and "More info" shows "Publisher: Unknown publisher".
  - Edge's download panel ignored my synthetic clicks. So for the double-click test I put Edge's mark on a copy myself rather than letting Edge finish the download.
- **UAC on every update.** The installer requires administrator rights:
  - `CreateProcessW("<installer> /S")` fails with error 740 ("requires elevation").
  - `ShellExecuteExW(open, "<installer>", "/S")` shows the UAC prompt.
  - I couldn't screenshot the prompt itself, because Windows draws it on a separate secure screen.
- **`/S` works.** A fresh install took 33 s, installed for all users into `C:\Program Files\JusPrin`, and does not reopen the app.
- **App still open:** the installer exited 0 and the registry says 2.0.1, but `orca-slicer.exe`, `OrcaSlicer.dll` and about 50 other DLLs stayed at 2.0.0 while the resources became 2.0.1. The app restarts fine in that mixed state. Running the installer again after quitting fixes it.
- **App just quit:** 45 s, exit 0, every file 2.0.1.
- **Helper flow:** the helper waited for the app's process to exit, ran `"<installer>" /S`, then `explorer.exe "C:\Program Files\JusPrin\orca-slicer.exe"`.
  - Timing: the app took 11 s to close, the install 136 s, and the window was back at 190 s.
  - During the install the person sees only the desktop.
  - The reopened app runs as the normal user, not as administrator.
  - `JusPrin2.conf` changed only in one temp-file path; the data folder has the same 1,841 files.
- **Install time varies:** 45 to 136 s for the same upgrade.
- **Full disk breaks it.** With 600 MB free, `/S` stopped halfway (exit 2) and left a half-copied folder with no uninstall entry.

**Inferred, not measured:** Windows 11's Smart App Control checks unsigned programs however they are started. This comes from secondary sources ([Eric Lawrence](https://textslashplain.com/2026/04/28/smart-app-control/), [SmartScreen practices](https://textslashplain.com/2024/11/15/best-practices-for-smartscreen-apprep/), [geekrewind](https://geekrewind.com/what-windows-11-smart-app-control-actually-blocks-and-how-to-disable-it/)); Windows Server doesn't have it. Separately, the app's `Http` code holds the whole 192 MB in memory before saving it.

**What a real version would need (my proposal, nothing decided):**
- A separate helper, kept outside the install folder, that waits for JusPrin's process to exit.
- A check after installing that `orca-slicer.exe` reports the new version, because the installer's exit code can't be trusted.
- Reopening the app through `explorer.exe`, so it doesn't run as administrator.
- A progress window, since nothing is on screen for 1–2.5 minutes.
- A free-space check before installing.
- Saving the download straight to a file instead of holding it in memory.
- A Windows code-signing certificate. Without one, UAC always says "Unknown publisher", and Smart App Control is likely to block the app. The upstream signing setup in `CMakeLists.txt` and `scripts/sign_windows.ps1` could be reused once there is a certificate.
- Removing the UAC prompt itself would mean changing to a per-user install, which is a bigger packaging change.

I didn't start the VM, and another session was using it, so I left it running. My test files and scheduled tasks are removed, and 2.0.1 is installed as it was when I started.

I put the test program back on the VM at `C:\guitest\ipr\updater_proto.exe`. It's the same build I used, and it writes a timed log to `C:\guitest\ipr\log.txt`. Below are four tests you can run yourself over Remote Desktop.

Before you start, two things about the VM. Another session may be using its screen, and Remote Desktop joins that same screen, so check nobody is mid-test. The VM has no graphics card, so JusPrin needs the Mesa graphics DLL copied into its folder after each install; the commands below include that.

## Connect

On your Mac, this prints the VM's address and the `guitest` password:

```bash
cd /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/vm-harness/windows && ./get-rdp-password.sh
```

Connect with Windows App as `guitest`.

## 1. Put 2.0.0 back

2.0.1 is installed now. Open an **administrator** PowerShell (right-click Start, then "Windows PowerShell (Admin)") and run:

```powershell
$d = "$env:TEMP\JusPrinUpdate"; mkdir $d -Force | Out-Null
$i0 = "$d\JusPrin_Windows_Installer_V2.0.0_x64.exe"
$i = "$d\JusPrin_Windows_Installer_V2.0.1_x64.exe"
curl.exe -L -o $i0 https://github.com/TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin/releases/download/jusprin/v2.0.0/JusPrin_Windows_Installer_V2.0.0_x64.exe
Start-Process $i0 -ArgumentList /S -Wait
mkdir "C:\Program Files\JusPrin\mesa" -Force | Out-Null; Copy-Item C:\guitest\mesa\opengl32.dll "C:\Program Files\JusPrin\mesa\"
(Get-Item "C:\Program Files\JusPrin\orca-slicer.exe").VersionInfo.FileVersion
```

The last line should print `2.0.0`. Keep this window open, because tests 3 and 4 use `$i`.

## 2. Download the way the app would

This test needs a **normal** PowerShell (from the Start menu, not "Admin"):

```powershell
cd C:\guitest\ipr
$d = "$env:TEMP\JusPrinUpdate"; $b = "https://github.com/TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin/releases/download/jusprin/v2.0.1"
.\updater_proto.exe download "$b/JusPrin_Windows_Installer_V2.0.1_x64.exe" "$d\JusPrin_Windows_Installer_V2.0.1_x64.exe"
.\updater_proto.exe download "$b/SHA256SUMS.txt" "$d\SHA256SUMS.txt"
.\updater_proto.exe verify "$d\JusPrin_Windows_Installer_V2.0.1_x64.exe" "$d\SHA256SUMS.txt"
Get-Item "$d\JusPrin_Windows_Installer_V2.0.1_x64.exe" -Stream *
.\updater_proto.exe run create "$d\JusPrin_Windows_Installer_V2.0.1_x64.exe" /S
.\updater_proto.exe run shell "$d\JusPrin_Windows_Installer_V2.0.1_x64.exe" /S
```

What you should see:
- The checksum line ends in `MATCH`.
- The file has only a `:$DATA` stream, meaning no "downloaded from the internet" mark.
- `run create` fails with error 740 ("requires elevation").
- `run shell` shows the UAC prompt with no SmartScreen step first. Click **No** so 2.0.0 stays installed.

## 3. The same file downloaded through Edge

1. In Edge, open `https://github.com/TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin/releases/download/jusprin/v2.0.1/JusPrin_Windows_Installer_V2.0.1_x64.exe`. Edge warns "isn't commonly downloaded".
2. In the download's "…" menu, choose Keep, then Show more, then Keep anyway.
3. Open the file from the Downloads folder. SmartScreen shows "Windows protected your PC". Click More info to see "Unknown publisher", then click Don't run.

## 4. Install while JusPrin is still open

1. Start JusPrin from the Start menu and wait for its window.
2. In the admin PowerShell, run:

```powershell
(Start-Process $i -ArgumentList /S -Wait -PassThru).ExitCode
(Get-ItemProperty HKLM:\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\JusPrin).DisplayVersion
(Get-Item "C:\Program Files\JusPrin\orca-slicer.exe").VersionInfo.FileVersion
```

You should get exit `0` and `2.0.1` in the registry, but the program file still reports `2.0.0`.

3. Quit JusPrin and run the same three lines again. All three should now report success and `2.0.1`. This is the "just quit" case, and it also repairs the mixed install.

## 5. The full flow: wait, install, reopen

1. Put 2.0.0 back with the `Start-Process $i0 …` and Mesa copy lines from step 1.
2. Start JusPrin from the Start menu.
3. In the admin PowerShell, start the helper. Running it from the admin window stands in for clicking Yes on UAC.

```powershell
$p = (Get-Process orca-slicer | Where-Object Path -like 'C:\Program Files\JusPrin\*').Id
Start-Process C:\guitest\ipr\updater_proto.exe -ArgumentList "helper $p `"$i`" `"C:\Program Files\JusPrin\orca-slicer.exe`""
```

4. Quit JusPrin. For one to two minutes you'll see only the desktop and the helper's console window; a real helper would have no window. Then JusPrin should reopen as 2.0.1 with the same projects and printer.
5. Read the timings in the log:

```powershell

```

If JusPrin doesn't open after an install, run the Mesa copy line from step 1 again. When you're done, delete `C:\guitest\ipr` and `$env:TEMP\JusPrinUpdate`. 2.0.1 will be left installed, as it was before.

"Prototype 'install and restart' for JusPrin on Windows… to learn its real cost and risks before deciding later." It asked for four things, each measured on the VM rather than inferred:

1. **A running JusPrin** downloads the 2.0.1 installer with the app's own `Slic3r::Http`, then starts it. Does Windows warn? Compare with the same file downloaded in Edge and double-clicked.
2. Does the installer accept `/S`? Does it work with JusPrin still running, just quit, and when it waits for the old process to exit? Does it ask for UAC, and where does it install?
3. Can the new version reopen automatically, as 2.0.1, with the same projects, printers, settings and sign-in?
4. The total time from pressing the button to the new version being open, and what the person sees along the way.

The brief allowed "a tiny standalone test program, or a debug hook in a local build".

## What I actually built

A standalone test program. It is not JusPrin, and JusPrin has no button. It compiles the app's `Http.cpp`, downloads the installer, checks the checksum, and can start the installer. A "helper" mode waits for a process to exit, installs, and reopens JusPrin. I ran these pieces separately, next to a real JusPrin 2.0.0.

## Where it falls short of the brief

- **The chain never ran as one piece.** Windows draws the UAC prompt on a screen my tools can't click. So "start the installer from a normal process → UAC → Yes → install" stopped at the prompt. Every real install ran from an administrator process standing in for "Yes". The 190 s timing has no UAC click in it and starts at the helper, not at a button.
- **The Edge comparison is partly simulated.** Edge did show its warning, but I couldn't finish the download by clicking. I wrote Edge's "downloaded from the internet" mark onto a copy myself, then opened that.
- **Sign-in wasn't tested.** The VM's data had an Anthropic API key, not a signed-in JusPrin account. I checked the settings file and project count, not whether you stay signed in.
- **"Comes up as 2.0.1" comes from the program file's version.** I didn't check it in the app's own screens.
- **Nothing in JusPrin starts anything.** Whether the app itself can quit cleanly with unsaved work, a running slice or an open dialog while a helper waits is untested.

What does hold: the Windows behaviour I measured. That covers error 740, UAC on every update, no SmartScreen for the file the app downloads, the success-but-mixed install when the app is open, and the clean install after it quits.

## Decision needed

How should we close those gaps, so the prototype is the real thing rather than parts of it?

- **Option A (my pick):** I add a temporary "Install update" item to a local JusPrin build on the VM, on a throwaway branch. It does download → checksum → start the helper with a UAC request → quit. Then you press it yourself over Remote Desktop and click Yes, and we time it from your click. That needs a JusPrin build on the VM, which is roughly 25–45 minutes of building because the VM's build folder is on another branch. It also tests the sign-in and app-quit cases properly.
- **Option B:** keep the current test program, but you click through the UAC prompt over Remote Desktop while I time it. That costs no building, but it still doesn't test JusPrin quitting itself or a button in the app.
- **Option C:** accept the current findings as enough to decide on, with the gaps listed above.

Which do you want?
Go with A

# Building JusPrin from source on the Windows VM

Verified 2026-09-07: full build from a clean VM, then run and screenshotted.
Total ~1h10m of machine time on n2-standard-16 (16 vCPU, 64 GB).

    deps build   22.7 min   (all 24 applicable deps from source)
    slicer build 23.0 min
    output       C:\src\JusPrin\build\src\Release\orca-slicer.exe (261 KB launcher)
                 + OrcaSlicer.dll (122.7 MB — the actual application)

## Order of operations

1. `install-buildtools.ps1` — CMake 4.3.5 (CI pins ~4.3.0), Ninja, Git for
   Windows, Strawberry Perl, and VS 2022 Build Tools with the VCTools workload.
2. Clone the repo (public, no credentials needed). Shallow is fine: the version
   comes from `version.inc`, not git tags.
3. `build-deps-full.ps1` — builds all deps. **Do not use the CI dependency
   artifact**; see below.
4. `build-slicer.ps1` — runs `build_release_vs.bat slicer`.
5. Put Mesa where the app looks for it, then `run-jusprin.cmd`.

## Things that will bite you

**Run long builds as a SCHEDULED TASK, not over SSH.** Windows OpenSSH kills the
whole process tree when the session ends, so a build started from an SSH command
(even detached with Start-Process) dies on disconnect. Register it instead:

    New-ScheduledTaskPrincipal -UserId "SYSTEM" -LogonType ServiceAccount -RunLevel Highest

Two builds racing in one directory corrupt each other — OpenSSL failed with
`C1033: cannot open program database ossl_static.pdb` when that happened here.

**awk must be on PATH.** `deps/PNG/PNG.cmake` passes `-DPNG_PREFIX=prusaslicer_`,
so libpng generates `pngprefix.h` with an awk script. Without awk you get
`AWK-NOTFOUND` in the PNG CMakeCache and then `C1083: Cannot open include file:
'pngprefix.h'`. Git for Windows ships awk — add `C:\Program Files\Git\usr\bin`
to PATH, not just `C:\Program Files\Git\cmd`.

**Set `CMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM=3.5`.** Several bundled CMakeLists still
declare pre-3.5 minimums, which CMake 4.x rejects outright.

**The CI dependency artifact is unusable.** `OrcaSlicer_dep_win64_20260906`
contains a bundle built 2025-10-17, before `deps/Eigen` was added. The source
requires Eigen 5.0.1 and CMake fails at configure with "Could not find a package
configuration file provided by Eigen3". Build deps from source instead.

**Never hard-stop the VM mid-build.** Stopping the instance during the deps build
left 622 of 22,011 installed files as NUL bytes. It surfaced as bogus syntax
errors deep in Boost headers. Detect it with:

    Get-ChildItem $prefix -Recurse -Include *.hpp,*.h,*.cmake |
      # read first 4 KB, flag any file containing byte 0

The fix is a clean rebuild; DL_CACHE keeps all 21 source archives, so it is a
recompile, not a re-download.

**Qhull is expected to be missing.** `deps/CMakeLists.txt` comments it out under
`if (MSVC)` ("Experimental"), so 24 built deps is the complete set on Windows.

## Running it — use the app's own Mesa hook

Do NOT drop opengl32.dll next to the exe. `src/OrcaSlicer_app_msvc.cpp` already
handles this: when system OpenGL is below 2.0 it loads `<exedir>\mesa\opengl32.dll`
itself and prints "MESA OpenGL library was loaded successfully".

    build\src\Release\mesa\opengl32.dll      <- Mesa's, the app loads this
    build\src\Release\libgallium_wgl.dll     <- dependency, resolves from exe dir

Still export `GALLIUM_DRIVER=llvmpipe` and `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1`: the GCE
virtual display exposes a D3D12 device, and Mesa's d3d12 backend crashes on the
first rendered frame.

## Windows CI is broken for a different reason

`Build all`'s Windows job fails at `cmake -G "Visual Studio 17 2022"` with
"could not find any instance of Visual Studio". That is NOT a bug in
`build_release_vs.bat` — the same script picks generator VS 17 2022 here from
`msbuild -version` (17.14.51.32402) and configures fine against a registered
Build Tools instance. The problem is the GitHub runner's environment.
$ErrorActionPreference = "Continue"
function Log($m) { $s = ("[SLICER {0:HH:mm:ss}] {1}" -f (Get-Date), $m); Write-Host $s; Add-Content C:\guitest\slicer-progress.txt $s }

$env:Path = [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable("Path","Machine")
$vswhere = "${env:ProgramFiles(x86)}\Microsoft Visual Studio\Installer\vswhere.exe"
$vsPath = & $vswhere -products * -requires Microsoft.VisualStudio.Component.VC.Tools.x86.x64 -property installationPath -latest
$env:Path = "$(Join-Path $vsPath 'MSBuild\Current\Bin');$env:Path"

Set-Content C:\guitest\slicer-progress.txt "slicer build starting $(Get-Date -Format o)"

Set-Location C:\src\JusPrin
$sw = [Diagnostics.Stopwatch]::StartNew()
& cmd /c "build_release_vs.bat slicer 2>&1" | Tee-Object -FilePath C:\guitest\slicer-build.log
$code = $LASTEXITCODE
$sw.Stop()

  Where-Object { $_.Length -gt 1MB } |
  ForEach-Object { Log ("  {0}  {1:N1} MB" -f $_.FullName, ($_.Length/1MB)) }
exit $code

---
name: side-session-wait-for-builds-silently
description: "A session started by another session must wait for a build in one quiet background command, not a Monitor that emits per compile step; each turn end wakes the parent."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 19893b9e-bc61-4b6a-98af-ef3116f46bd4
  modified: 2026-11-12T18:04:50.556Z
---

When a session started by another session waits on a long build, wait with one
`run_in_background` command that loops until ninja's PID exits, then run the
tests and report once. Do not use a Monitor whose filter matches per-file
compile lines (for example a test target's name): every event ends a turn, and
every turn end is relayed to the parent session and wakes it.

**Why:** On 2026-11-12 the handshake-banner session's Monitor matched
`agent_bridge_tests` and produced ~40 one-line turns; the parent ("Debug
session") asked it to stop reporting every build step.

**How to apply:** In side sessions, one background wait per build, and a Monitor
only for failure lines (`FAILED|error:`), never for progress. See
[[pkill-cmake-build-leaves-ninja]] for the build rules.

2. **A visible desktop.** A GUI app started from an SSH shell lands in a session

3. **Session isolation.** Display APIs, EnumWindows and Get-Process MainWindowTitle
   only see the CALLING session's window station. Run them over SSH and they
   silently report nothing — which reads as "the app has no window" when it does.
   Everything that touches the UI goes through `Invoke-InSession` in harness.ps1,
   which registers a scheduled task with `-LogonType Interactive` so it runs in
   session 1, and writes its output to a file to be read back over SSH.

#!/bin/bash
# Print the current RDP credentials for the Windows test VM, and verify they work.
#
# The password is stored in plaintext at Winlogon\DefaultPassword - that is how
# Windows auto-logon works - so this READS the live value rather than resetting
# it. A reset would invalidate a session that is currently working.
#
# The external IP is ephemeral and changes on every stop/start, so resolve it
# from GCE rather than trusting a hardcoded value.
#
# Note on quoting: PowerShell is invoked via -EncodedCommand. Passing a script
# inline through ssh into `powershell -Command` mangles nested quotes; encoding
# removes the problem entirely.
set -euo pipefail

INSTANCE=jusprin-win-test
ZONE=us-central1-a
PROJECT=elegoo-backend
VMUSER=guitest
KEY=~/.ssh/google_compute_engine

gcloud config set account ai-agent@tsdtechnology.iam.gserviceaccount.com >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

STATUS=$(gcloud compute instances describe "$INSTANCE" --zone="$ZONE" --project="$PROJECT" \
    --format="value(status)")
if [ "$STATUS" != "RUNNING" ]; then
    echo "VM is $STATUS. Start it with:"
    echo "  gcloud compute instances start $INSTANCE --zone=$ZONE --project=$PROJECT"
    exit 1
fi

The code is commit cc69feae92 on the local branch `proto/win-install-restart-from-2.0.0`, based on the 2.0.0 tag. It is not pushed, and it is in a worktree on my Mac and a separate one on the VM.

**What my dry run showed:**
- I pressed Download at 19:16:04 VM time. A progress window appeared, the 192 MB installer downloaded in 9 s, and its checksum matched the release's published list.
- 10.4 s after the click, the Windows admin-rights prompt appeared. I can't click that prompt from here, so I stopped there.
- When the prompt is cancelled, JusPrin says "The update was cancelled. JusPrin was not changed." and keeps running.

**Your click-through:**
1. On your Mac, run this. It prints the VM's address and the `guitest` password:
```bash
/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/vm-harness/windows/get-rdp-password.sh
```
2. Connect with Remote Desktop as `guitest`. JusPrin 2.0.0 is open at Home with 4 projects and the Anker M5. Behind it is an old PowerShell window from an hour ago, which you can close. It shows someone, probably you, running my earlier manual steps, which were broken: the installer file was never saved.
3. Optional, before pressing:
   - To test whether sign-in survives the update, sign in under the gear icon › Account.
   - To test what happens to unsaved work, open a project and change something without saving.
4. Click the gear icon, then Updates, then **Download**.
   - The note beside the button still says "Opens the release page on GitHub". That page wasn't rebuilt, so ignore the note.
   - "Full release notes on GitHub" also starts the install in this build.
5. After about 10 s the admin prompt appears. Click **Yes**.
6. JusPrin closes. Expect nothing on screen for roughly 1 to 2.5 minutes while the installer runs, then JusPrin 2.0.1 should open.

A watcher on the VM is recording the timeline: every JusPrin window, the admin prompt and the installer, to the millisecond, for the next three hours. When you're done, I'll read it and work out:
- the time from your click to the new window;
- whether the installed program is really 2.0.1;
- whether your projects, printer, settings and sign-in survived;
- what happened to the unsaved project.

Then I'll write the report.

**One VM-only step:** after the install, the helper program also copies the software-graphics DLL back into the JusPrin folder, because this VM has no graphics card. A real updater wouldn't do that.

Builds on [[live-host-check-via-instrumented-dev-page]]; used 2026-11-02 when screen control of the app was denied.

- Signed-in conf needs all of: `jusprin_agent.{provider=jusprin, jusprin_api_key, enabled=true, cloud_consent=true, jusprin_model_formats=<JSON id→format from GET /ent/jusprin/v2/models>}`, `jusprin_server.base_url`, `jusprin_onboarding.status=completed`. Without the formats the Agent says "not set up".
- An installed printer is `"models":[{"vendor":"Custom","model":"Generic Klipper Printer","nozzle_diameter":"0.4"}]`, not `vendors`.
- Kill the app before editing the conf. Replace a scratch binary with `rm` then `cp`: `cp` over a binary that has run gets the new process killed at launch.
- `Contents/Resources` in the build is a symlink to the worktree. Replace it with a real folder of links before corrupting a resource, or the worktree gets corrupted.
- Bringing the app forward triggers an account refresh, so to race the gateway (a real 402), change the ledger and send without refocusing.
- Page text input: native value setter plus an `input` event. A modal Preferences window's page polls as `agent-preferences`.
- A test preset needs a `version` field or import rejects it.
- A compose recreate drops env set by a wrapper; check `JUSPRIN_MODEL_ALIASES` before any chat so only the fake upstream is reachable.

Still needs the screen: pointer hover, native file dialogs, Orca's wizard.

content.text:
Your run worked. It took 69 seconds from your click on Download to the JusPrin 2.0.1 window, and you clicked the Windows admin prompt once. Everything afterwards is 2.0.1, and your projects, printer and settings came through unchanged.

**What happened, in seconds after your click** (measured from the shared timeline the app, the helper and the window watcher all write to):

| Seconds | What happened |
|---|---|
| 0 | A progress window showed "Downloading JusPrin 2.0.1…" |
| 9.2 | The 192 MB installer finished downloading |
| 10.6 | Its checksum matched, and the Windows admin prompt appeared |
| 16.8 | You clicked Yes, and JusPrin's windows closed within half a second |
| 17.9 to 57.1 | The installer ran for 39 s with nothing on screen |
| 69.4 | JusPrin 2.0.1 opened |

**Checked afterwards:**
- The uninstall entry and `orca-slicer.exe` both say 2.0.1, and the app's own log names the 2.0.1 release build.
- The reopened JusPrin runs as a normal user, not as administrator.
- It shows the same 4 projects, the Anker M5, the Anthropic key and the same settings.

**Not covered by this run:**
- **Sign-in:** the app was still using the Anthropic key, not a JusPrin account, so I don't know yet whether a signed-in account survives.
- **Unsaved work:** the project had no unsaved changes, so I don't know what happens to unsaved work when the app quits for the update.

I added these results and the timeline to `REPORT.md` in the shared notes folder.

**About the gap with nothing on screen:** on this VM it was 39 s, and earlier runs took 45 to 136 s. I haven't tried either fix yet, so these are estimates.

1. **The installer shows its own progress bar.** The installer already has a progress page; `/S` hides it. We could run it with every other page skipped, so the person sees only "Installing JusPrin…" with a real bar, and it closes itself at the end.
   - My guess is this is the better result, because the bar reflects actual progress.
   - The catch: the installer script is generated by CMake's packaging tool from its own template, and that template adds the pages. To skip each one, we would probably need our own copy of the template, which is more to maintain.
2. **The helper shows its own small window.** The helper is our own program, so it can show "Installing JusPrin 2.0.1…" with a progress bar. It would estimate progress by counting files written into the install folder against about 18,900 expected.
   - This should be a small change, perhaps a day.
   - The catch: the bar is an estimate, not the installer's real progress.

I'd try the second first, because it leaves the installer alone, and fall back to the first if the estimated bar looks wrong. To answer "how difficult" with evidence rather than a guess, I'd build both on the VM and time them.
Yes, prototype it

uninst:

  StrCmp $2 "$\"" 0 +2  # if char is quote

uses: microsoft/setup-msbuild@v3

      # NSIS builds the installer. A pinned portable copy is kept in the Actions
      # cache, so most runs never download it, and a cache miss fetches the
      # release archive from SourceForge instead of going through the Chocolatey
      # community feed, which hosted runners often cannot reach. Prepending it to
      # PATH also makes cpack use it over the NSIS preinstalled on some images.
      - name: Restore NSIS
        id: nsis-cache
        if: runner.os == 'Windows' && !vars.SELF_HOSTED
        uses: actions/cache/restore@v6
        with:
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/nsis
          key: nsis-${{ env.NSIS_VERSION }}

      - name: Install NSIS
        if: runner.os == 'Windows' && !vars.SELF_HOSTED
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          dir "C:/Program Files (x86)/Windows Kits/10/Include"
          $nsisDir = Join-Path $env:RUNNER_TEMP 'nsis'
          $makensis = Join-Path $nsisDir 'makensis.exe'
          if (-not (Test-Path $makensis)) {
            $zip = Join-Path $env:RUNNER_TEMP "nsis-$env:NSIS_VERSION.zip"
            curl.exe -fsSL --retry 5 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 15 -o $zip "https://downloads.sourceforge.net/project/nsis/NSIS%203/$env:NSIS_VERSION/nsis-$env:NSIS_VERSION.zip"
            if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "NSIS $env:NSIS_VERSION download failed." }
            if ((Get-FileHash $zip -Algorithm SHA256).Hash -ne $env:NSIS_SHA256) {
              throw "NSIS $env:NSIS_VERSION archive does not match its pinned SHA256."
            }
            Expand-Archive $zip $env:RUNNER_TEMP
            Move-Item (Join-Path $env:RUNNER_TEMP "nsis-$env:NSIS_VERSION") $nsisDir
          }
          & $makensis /VERSION
          $nsisDir | Out-File -Append -FilePath $env:GITHUB_PATH -Encoding utf8

cat >> src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/installer.nsh <<'EOF'

; THROWAWAY PROTOTYPE: "/PASSIVE" on the command line shows only the progress
; page, then reopens JusPrin and closes. JusPrin's updater runs the installer
; this way so the person sees the install happen without answering any page.
; CPack's template inserts the pages; this include comes before them, so the
; define below attaches to the first page (Welcome) only. Its show function
; jumps straight to the progress page, past the pages in between.
!include "FileFunc.nsh"
Var JusPrinPassive
!define MUI_PAGE_CUSTOMFUNCTION_SHOW JusPrinWelcomeShow
Function JusPrinWelcomeShow
  ${GetParameters} $R0
  ClearErrors
  ${GetOptions} $R0 "/PASSIVE" $R1
  IfErrors jusprin_not_passive
  StrCpy $JusPrinPassive 1
  SendMessage $HWNDPARENT 0x408 ${JUSPRIN_PASSIVE_JUMP} 0
jusprin_not_passive:
FunctionEnd

; Called at the end of the install section (CPACK_NSIS_EXTRA_INSTALL_COMMANDS).
!macro JusPrinPassiveFinish
  StrCmp $JusPrinPassive 1 0 +3
    Call JusPrinRun
    Quit
!macroend
EOF

  ClearErrors

    SetShellVarContext all

  !insertmacro SectionList "FinishSection"

!ifdef CPACK_NSIS_ADD_REMOVE
  ; Get the name of the installer executable
  System::Call 'kernel32::GetModuleFileNameA(i 0, t .R0, i 1024) i r1'
  StrCpy $R3 $R0

  ; Strip off the last 13 characters, to see if we have AddRemove.exe
  StrLen $R1 $R0
  IntOp $R1 $R0 - 13
  StrCpy $R2 $R0 13 $R1
  StrCmp $R2 "AddRemove.exe" addremove_installed

  ; We're not running AddRemove.exe, so install it
  CopyFiles $R3 $INSTDIR\AddRemove.exe

  addremove_installed:
!endif
SectionEnd
